Bug_Details:
== NaN always returns false; use the isNaN methods instead As per JLS 15.21.1, == NaN comparisons always return false, even NaN == NaN.
Instead, use the isNaN methods to check for NaN.
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by using the '==' operator to compare a double value with Double.NaN. According to the JLS 15.21.1, this comparison will always return false, even when comparing NaN with itself.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBugWithNaN' triggers the bug by calling the'showBug' method with Double.NaN as the argument. The method uses the '==' operator to compare the input value with Double.NaN, which always returns false according to the Java Language Specification (JLS 15.21.1). The test case expects the method to return true for NaN, causing the test to fail and thus trigger the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test method 'testShowBugWithNaN' uses assertFalse to assert that the method'showBug' returns false when given Double.NaN, which confirms the bug since the comparison 'value == Double.NaN' always returns false, even for NaN.
